harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Configured node1 so only root and opsadmin can schedule cron jobs. The configuration and cron service persisted across a verified node restart without changing Ubuntu 7.10 or kernel 2.6.22-14-generic.
actions_performed: Created the locked local opsadmin account.
Created /etc/cron.allow containing exactly root and opsadmin, owned by root:crontab with mode 0640 for compatibility with the legacy setgid crontab client.
Proved root and opsadmin could install, list, and remove a harmless probe crontab; proved nobody was denied.
Restarted node1 exactly once and verified recovery with a changed boot ID.

evidence.requirement: Only root and opsadmin may schedule cron jobs
evidence.summary: The allowlist contains exactly root and opsadmin. Both permitted users successfully exercised crontab installation; nobody was explicitly denied. The policy remained enforced after restart.

evidence.requirement: Keep the installed operating-system release and kernel
evidence.summary: Ubuntu 7.10 and kernel 2.6.22-14-generic were unchanged before and after configuration and restart.

Healthy pre-restart boot ID was 1e345705-924b-4844-a423-aa4db2927c53; the reboot was acknowledged; post-restart boot ID changed to dadc9e36-69d1-4139-b0ff-a5711c41e128; cron, the account, exact allowlist, and access enforcement all recovered.

attempts.summary: Configured node1 so only root and opsadmin can schedule cron jobs. The configuration and cron service persisted across a verified node restart without changing Ubuntu 7.10 or kernel 2.6.22-14-generic.
